frontier.hypothesis: PRIMARY. An insn counted by flow, still present through global_alloc, and deleted AFTER it (reload's no-op-move deletion, or jump2's cross-jumping / no-op-move deletion) is simultaneously a counted reference and byte-free — exactly the shape out2's missing reference needs, and the only surface in this grind no session has probed.
frontier.mechanism: global_alloc reads reg_n_refs and reg_live_length before reload, sched2, jump2 and reorg run, so every closure in this ledger (which stops at combine and local-alloc) leaves this surface untested. s34's E-s34-3 sharpens the requirement: the deleted insn must mention out2 and must NOT hand that occurrence to a surviving emitted insn — i.e. a copy that becomes a no-op because both pseudos land on the same hard register, or an insn tail that jump2 cross-jumps away.
frontier.next_probe: Do the cheapest falsification FIRST: on the already-dumped L1/D5 chassis, diff red.i.greg against red.i.jump2 and red.i.dbr and see whether ANY insn disappears after .greg in this function at all. If none does, the item closes in one read. If some do, spell (a) a loop1-local copy `tmp = out2;` whose consumer forces tmp onto out2's own seat and check red.i.greg for the shared hard register, and (b) two textually identical loop1 statement tails so jump2 cross-jumps one away with out2 mentioned in the deleted copy. Harness: tmp/grind/func_80041188/s34/run.ps1 plus s34/dump.sh <TAG> and s33/fr.sh <TAG> 86 87.

frontier.hypothesis: A combine deletion whose out2 occurrence SIMPLIFIES AWAY is the one escape from E-s28-2's conservation law, and would give a flow-counted, byte-free reference inside loop1.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c try_combine -> subst -> simplify_rtx folds `(minus X X)`, `(and X (not X))` and friends to constants at substitution time. flow ran before combine, so the reference is already counted, and the occurrence is gone from the emitted insn.
frontier.next_probe: The blocking question is SEMANTIC and must be answered before any measurement: enumerate loop1's ten statements against the named data layout (E-s33-2: stptr walks 0x68-byte records, tbl walks a s32 table, p/buf stage six halfwords, the two matrices are &m[0] and &m[1]) and ask whether any of them can honestly consume a difference or cancellation involving &m[1]. If none can, this item closes on exactly the grounds E-s33-3 used for block 2 — and that closure would leave frontier 1 as the last open surface in the entire grind, which is itself the result worth banking.

frontier.hypothesis: The +2 insns E-s31-3 measured for the pre-test loop1 (the only construct that stops cse2's fold) were priced on a chassis WITHOUT the sanctioned split-increment lifts; on the E-s34-3 ladder those two insns may be recoverable, in which case the CODE_LABEL family reopens.
frontier.mechanism: H1/H2/H3 emit an unconditional `j` plus its delay slot at loop1's bottom in addition to the exit test. E-s27-2's D6 shows this function has at least one absorbable slot: at one re-store position sched1 hoists `addiu $a0,$sp,0x10` into loop1's load-delay slot and target's own nop at asm/funcs/func_80041188.s:30 disappears, paying for a surplus insn out of a nop and returning the build to 132 insns.
frontier.next_probe: Measure H1 (D5 + pre-test loop1, previously 135 insns / sandbox 22) with the re-store moved to D6's position and the full E-s34-3 lift set applied, and read the INSN COUNT rather than the score. The item is alive only if the count falls to 133 or below; if it stays at 134+, strike the CODE_LABEL family from the ledger for good.
